_meta.target: DJI Phantom 3 Professional (WM331) — mesh rebuilt from photographs
_meta.what_changed: Until today drone_cad's phantom3 shape tables were phantom4's, because the repository held no Phantom 3 photograph. assets/photos/phantom3/ now holds 145 reference images. This round measured what those images can measure and replaced the inherited constants. Nothing here was chosen by looking at an RCS number: the fit coefficients in outputs/p3_ours.json were not opened while measuring.
code: src/drone_cad.py :: _SHELL_SHAPE['phantom3'], _ARM_WIDTH, _ARM_SECTION, GEAR_ARCH, INTERNALS, MOTOR_BASE_Z, ARM_TIP_OVERHANG, build_frame_cad phantom3 gimbal branch
_meta.figure: outputs/figs/p3_mesh_v2.png (new mesh above, old mesh below, same camera and scale)

grades.M: measured on a Phantom 3 image, pixel scale recorded
grades.D: derived from Phantom 3 measurements or from a published Phantom 3 figure
grades.H: no Phantom 3 evidence — shared repository law or a judgement call

front_elevation.anchor_1: motor bell centres 330.3 px apart = 2*(350/2)*sin45 = 247.49 mm
front_elevation.anchor_2: shell crown row 347.1 to feet row 594 = 246.9 px = published 185 mm
front_elevation.cross_check: the two anchors agree to five digits (0.749289 vs 0.749291)

rear_elevation.cross_check: crown 650.3 to feet 896 = 245.7 px = 185.4 mm (+0.2 % of published)

official_top_render.cross_check: the two diagonals measure 727.6 and 727.0 px, 0.08 % apart

headline_correction.claim: The published 185 mm is the SHELL CROWN to the feet, not the motor top to the feet.
evidence: front elevation: crown row 347.1 -> feet 594 = 246.9 px x 0.74929 = 184.1 mm
rear elevation: crown row 650.3 -> feet 896 = 245.7 px x 0.75457 = 185.4 mm
motor bell top is row 361 in the front elevation, i.e. 10.4 mm BELOW the crown; motor top to feet is only 175.0 mm
headline_correction.what_it_overturns: outputs/p3_specs.json measured_from_manufacturer_drawing recorded shell_crown_to_belly = 63.9 mm and belly_to_foot = 120.5 mm by taking the motor top as the crown. The true split is shell 78.6 mm and legs 111.6 mm (foot pad radius takes gear_h_mm to 106.1). That JSON has not been edited here; this file is the correction record.
headline_correction.consequence: the envelope forcing (None, None, 185) is now nearly inert — frame_fit_scale sz went from 0.9565 to 0.9982, so the mesh is no longer squashed 4.4 % vertically to meet the published height.

body_x_offset_mm.note: the shell sits 14.8 mm AFT of the rotor centre; new _SHELL_SHAPE key bx0

half_width_profile_mm.note: armpit envelope; beyond |x| ~ 35 mm the 45 deg arm covers it, so those values are the arm outline, not the body

chord_vs_radius_mm.src: d03 top, perpendicular chords on the 45 deg ray, 4 arms averaged

section_h_ratio.src: front elevation: pod 16.3 mm tall on 31 mm wide, root 20.6 on 43

tip_overhang_beyond_motor_axis_mm.src: solved from the published 289.0 mm plan width with the 350 mm diagonal and the 31 mm tip width

motor.cross_check: DJI publishes the 2312 stator as 23 x 12 mm; a 28.3 mm aluminium bell around it is consistent

belly_to_foot_mm.note: gear_h_mm is 106.1 because the skid capsule adds its 5.5 mm radius below

landing_gear.shape: a closed rectangular loop (top bar, two struts, bottom skid) — confirmed on phantom3_c06_ifixit_std_landing_gear_pair.jpg. It tapers strongly fore-aft: 162 mm at the top, 104 mm at the feet. The phantom4 legs are nearly parallel.

camera_bottom_above_feet_mm.note: the feet, not the camera, are the lowest point

x_position_mm.note: the gimbal hangs near the AIRCRAFT CENTRE, not under the nose. p33 puts the damper-plate centre 26 mm forward of the rotor centre, the side elevation +5 mm. The old code used nose_x*0.62 = +46 mm, an inherited value.

internal_scatterers.note: 3 boxes x (3 sizes + 3 positions). These were the never-measured ones.

src: rear elevation: exposed rear face 76.1 x 46.6 mm (the face with the 4 LEDs and the power button)
d03 top: 74.6 mm wide, rear face at x = -89.6
p33 bottom: bay floor 766 px = 80.2 mm long
battery.volume_check: 76 x 45 x 80 = 274 mL for 68 Wh = 248 Wh/L, right for a cased 4S pouch pack; a 120 mm length would give 0.85 g/mL, too light for LiPo

centre_x_board.src: t67 shell-off top-down: bbox 159 (lateral) x 128 (fore-aft) mm
centre_x_board.declared_simplification: the real board is X-shaped and does not fill that bbox. We use an area-equivalent rectangle inside it, because the 'pcb' group is NOT in build_frame_cad's boolean union list, so two crossed plates would leave buried faces for PO/SBR to count.

shielded_video_module.src: t67: 210 x 160 px = 44 x 33 mm; height ~20 mm from the oblique t29
shielded_video_module.replaces: the magnesium structural plate that the shared shell-v2 path inserted. THE PHANTOM 3 HAS NO MAGNESIUM SKELETON (that is the Phantom 4's headline structural change), so the old mesh was over-metalling the fuselage with a part that does not exist.

items.what: _SHELL_SHAPE npow (superellipse exponent of the body cross-section)
items.why: a photograph of a smooth white shell does not resolve how square the section is. Set to 3.0 by judgement; phantom4 uses 3.4.

items.what: _body_folding law: the six station x-fractions, tail_w 0.95, n_sec 30, n_pts 72, Taubin iters 4
items.why: shared repository law for every shell airframe, not a per-airframe measurement

items.what: _canopy internal law (4 stations x half-width/half-height, n_pow, z = 0.30 H)
items.why: the Phantom 3 has no raised canopy at all. Only the canopy's placement and size were set from the battery bay; its internal shape law is untouched and now sits buried inside the body.

items.what: arm tip rise z1 = 0.012*diag and the Bezier bend 0.02
items.why: the drawing shows the arm rising toward the motor but the two literals are not separable from it
only the bell's outer diameter and height are visible in an elevation; its waist and shoulder are not

items.what: _gear_arch corner radius 0.004 m and the sweep resolutions
propeller H-grade law (sweep_frac 0.10, root_frac, hub 0.085R x 0.09R, resolutions, base_ang 12 deg, spin direction)
items.why: shared prop law anchored on three reference propellers, not on this aircraft. The 9450 is the same part number the phantom4 entry uses.

items.what: propeller D-grade law (chord max over R, thickness ratios, camber)
group -> material assignment for the 8 groups present

items.why: materials.py is the single source; no Phantom 3 measurement exists

items.what: shell transmission convention (which group is shell, tau = 1 - |Gamma|^2)

cannot_measure: Body half-width and half-height at the two stations the arms cover (model x = -59.7 and +42.0). A 45 deg arm 43 mm wide hides the shell there in every view we have; those four numbers are smooth interpolations between the neighbouring measurements.
The superellipse exponent of the body cross-section (npow). No view resolves it.
The gimbal camera block's fore-aft depth to better than a few mm — the side elevation shows 31.9 mm of block plus an unresolved lens mount; 34 mm is the working value.
Motor internals. Only the bell's outside is visible; DJI publishes the stator as 23 x 12 mm but not the bell wall thickness or the magnet ring.
Propeller aerofoil section for the DJI 9450. Our blade law comes from three other propellers; no 9450 section was measured.
Material grades. DJI never published the shell polymer, and no Phantom 3 dielectric measurement exists.

Prop mounting height. The house formula prop_z = motor_h + arm_t/2 + 6 mm gives 33.7 mm where the drawing shows the blade plane at 27.7 mm. Fixing it needs a spec-level prop_z override that would touch every airframe, so the 6 mm is recorded, not patched.
Whether the aircraft in the measurement literature wore the stock polymer 9450 or DJI's optional carbon-fibre-reinforced 9450 (+11.1 dB on the propeller group). Unchanged from the previous round.
The variant actually measured in the literature. Unchanged: all Phantom 3 variants share one shell, so this does not move the geometry.

sanity.mesh_check: every group passes: watertight per connected part, no inward normals, no winding breaks, no degenerate faces. body 7792 faces in ONE part (arms fuse into the shell), camera 6 parts, gear 2, motor 4, prop 4, battery 2, pcb 1, canopy 1.

silhouette_iou.method: src/viz_mesh_photo.py, unchanged pipeline and unchanged registered photo set, run once on the old mesh and once on the new one

independent_check_without_any_pose_fitti.what: frame silhouette vs the official top render, scale and centre fixed by the published 350 mm diagonal, no camera fitted at all

silhouette_iou.circularity_warning: phantom3_d03_official_top.png is BOTH a measurement source (plan form, arm widths, hub radius) and a scoring photograph, so its 0.582 is partly self-graded. This is the same situation the repository already records for s1000plus, and the same one that applies to phantom4 / mini5pro / mavic4pro, whose shell tables were measured on their own registered photographs. The headline photograph here is d02 (front), whose aspect was measured from a different file (the manual's orthographic front elevation, m01), so the circularity is partial, not total.
silhouette_iou.ledger_note: outputs/mesh_compare_photo.json was NOT rewritten — viz_mesh_photo.build_all replaces the whole ledger and only phantom3 was run. Both runs were done in scratch copies of the repository.

biggest_changes: Published 185 mm re-read as shell crown to feet: shell 63.9 -> 78.6 mm (+23 %), legs 120.5 -> 111.6 mm.
Plan form measured for the first time: body 149.6 x 138.9 mm sitting 14.8 mm aft of the rotor centre, with the measured waist. The inherited phantom4 body was 175 x 158 mm and centred.
Frame bbox 283.9 -> 289.07 mm, i.e. the published 289.5 x 289.0 is now met to 0.15 %, and the vertical envelope squash dropped from 4.4 % to 0.2 %.
Motor bell 36.4 -> 28.3 mm diameter (the diagonal-proportional fallback was +29 %).
Gimbal moved 24 mm aft to its measured position near the aircraft centre, and rebuilt from four measured parts instead of the shared hanging-gimbal ratio law.
Landing gear rebuilt: 9.3 x 14.2 mm struts (was 13 x 24), foot track 166.3 mm, and the strongly tapered fore-aft loop the drawing shows.
Internal scatterers measured for the first time: battery 80 x 76 x 45 mm at the tail, centre X board 120 x 110 mm at the arm plane, shielded video module 44 x 33 x 20 mm.
The magnesium structural plate was removed. The Phantom 3 has no magnesium skeleton; the shared shell-v2 path had been inserting one.
